Congratulations! Here's some more unsolicited advice, but I won't rehash what everyone already said :P

Some first trimester symptoms that are common and relevant to you:

She's likely to be extremely fatigued, even though she isn't visibly pregnant yet. The energy demands in the beginning are enormous, and she'll likely need naps, and help keeping up with basic, routine tasks for a while. She'll likely get her energy back in the second trimester.

She may be more irritable than normal, and escalate to anger rapidly. If she is aware this is a normal symptom of the hormones, she may be able to control her reactions better. This also reduced for me in the second trimester, thankfully.

Heightened sense of smell, nausea and food aversions. How bad these are will vary from person to person, and even from one pregnancy to the next. The food aversions are often to really stupid, annoying things, too, like meat and the smell of cooking food. Eating decent food is another thing she may need help with in the first trimester, because of this and the fatigue. Grass fed whole milk was a lifesaver for me with the nausea, both for easing the nausea and for getting down something with food value when selections were difficult. I do raw milk, but if she doesn't already drink raw, she probably won't want to start while pregnant.

Food/supplement recommendations besides milk:

I also recommend any naturally probiotic foods she can stomach, like yogurt, kefir, kombucha, water kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi, old fashioned brined pickles. Pregnancy slows digestion, and these help speed it back up, they contain the animal form of vitamin K, and improve the microbiome she will pass to the baby. They're also good for kidney and liver function and stuff. Water kefir is a good alternative to kombucha if the vinegar flavor of kombucha bothers her.

Roasted dandelion root tea also helps with digestion, and it helps the liver process excess hormones, I think it has helped me control my mood swings. Some honey will cut the bitterness and make it taste more peanut buttery. Green tea shares some of these benefits.

Cod liver oil is an excellent source of the animal forms of vitamins A & D and essential fatty acids, which she will need a lot of to grow a baby with a healthy brain, symmetrical bone structure, and good eyesight. Synthetic forms of vitamin A are not absorbed well and can cause birth defects in large amounts. Plant forms of vitamin A are not absorbed or converted well, so if her vitamin says it has a ton of vitamin A as beta carotine, that's NOT how much actual vitamin A she's getting, it's maybe a tenth of that. I've been using the Garden of Life brand Lemon Mint flavor and have had no problems with it triggering nausea/gag reflex unlike brands I've tried before, but it can also be mixed into some juice for flavor and texture.

Calcium antagonizes the absorption of iron and zinc. This gets important toward the end of the second trimester/beginning of the third when she is increasing her blood volume by about half while the baby is ossifying its skeleton. A prenatal that contains all of these together isn't going to get her enough iron and calcium. Try to leave a few hours between iron supplements and calcium supplements to improve absorption. Heme iron, the form of iron found in meat, is much better absorbed than plant forms in the presence of calcium. Foot and leg cramps will be stopped by a good calcium magnesium citrate supplement, up the dose if they start again later.
